findings: Complete current MDX SHA-256 is 5bb086a5bcf86e58204afd9491530a445b380aa2760995f84676b3eb4ffb30c2; all 5 declared sources passed current HTTPS access review.
Claims are bounded to five official sources: the 2025 Midland CAD Mass Appraisal Report, current Publications, Open Records, and Mineral Property pages, and the Texas Comptroller Midland directory.

The official report is a 392,040-byte, 35-page PDF with SHA-256 18f2c391a8618b1713280f7d2dfa3f78c0f5770c924133314d9e8c0636b5e1a2; physical PDF page 25 was independently extracted and visually reviewed.

The physical-page-25 rendering has SHA-256 197d45c775b70fc23ea92ece9943c2ae34669e8fbe5b28b38c535b7836fce439 and shows the statement that industrial appraisers are responsible for the valuation of 419,660 mineral interest accounts.
The report uses approximately before the count, and the article retains that qualifier rather than silently normalizing the statement into an exact current inventory.

The controlled Publications, Open Records, Mineral Property, and Comptroller directory artifacts have SHA-256 values ecfab3416d57144355170bdea0d5dbfcc087ee932bdae62c0da46545d7d987de, 9a5465430a510a716ab162a0ad2287ea83da12d677bd17456ef525272d4af482, dbab9120e18eb86b81130445a5aa12aa959ca5a0af162ba2847248bee58ce1d5, and 236fb5f5686a90b91c02047d50361f8639c498facad7ecb4cc3d973f6e28d813.
No owner, property, account, roll, notice, or mineral-file search was performed and no record was reproduced.
